title: Pico Kit: Fast Onboard Playbook (sketch)
content:
TL;DR: A trimmed "Pico Kit" that gets a new engineer or small partner integration from zero to an instrumented sample app in ~10 minutes (local) and ~30 minutes (deployed). This doc is a lightweight playbook for product-first bootstraps: short checklist, reproducible commands, minimal telemetry, and clear gating for handing to solutions engineering.

Purpose
- Reduce friction for first 10 minutes with Redwood SDKs and API.
- Provide a single, opinionated path that covers: install, auth, run a sample request, basic telemetry, and a safety/fallback test.
- Serve as a handoff artifact for SEs to run guided demos.

Scope
- Audience: new hires (engineers), partner SEs doing demo integrations, small internal PoCs.
- Platforms: macOS/Linux (local dev), optional Docker for hermetic runs.
- Not in scope: full CI/CD, production deployment templates, enterprise-only private VPC setup (separate doc).

Outcome (what success looks like)
- Developer can run sample app and see streamed response and token-level cost breakdown in console.
- Instrumentation: request id, latency, tokens emitted (sample telemetry).
- Basic failure mode: SDK falling back to a compatible smaller model when quota/capacity error is simulated.

Design principles (short)
- Minimal cognitive overhead: 5–7 commands, friendly UX messages.
- Observable by default: default sample app logs request ids and key metrics.
- Safe: include an example of short prompt to avoid unsafe outputs and sample guardrail.
- Reproducible: pinned example package versions to avoid flakiness.

Pico Kit contents
- README-mini.md (single-page quickstart)
- sample-app (tiny Node + Python examples)
- run-local.sh and run-docker.sh
- smoke-check.sh (automated smoke tests)
- telemetry-mapping.md (what we collect in the sample)
- checklist-for-demo (one-pager for SE)

Quickstart (10 minutes local)
1) Prereqs
   - Node 18+ or Python 3.10+ installed
   - A Redwood API key (REDWOOD_API_KEY) or free trial flags (instructions below)
2) Grab the Pico kit
   - git clone https://github.com/redwood-inference/pico-kit && cd pico-kit
   - git checkout stable-compact-2025-01
3) Install (Node example)
   - cd node-sample
   - npm ci --silent
4) Set creds
   - export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-live-... (or run cred-helper script)
5) Run sample server (dev mode)
   - npm start  # starts express server with /chat endpoint
6) Try the quick request
   - curl -s -X POST http://localhost:3000/chat -d '{"prompt":"Summarize the following commit: add tests for caching"}' | jq .
   - Expected: JSON with "response", "request_id", "tokens_used" fields
7) Observe telemetry
   - tail -f logs/pico-kit.log  # shows request-id, latency, model variant
8) Run smoke check (automated)
   - ./smoke-check.sh  # will fail if token counts missing or fallback not exercised
Example minimal Node snippet (already in sample)
- shows pragmatic use: set API key, call client.chat.create, stream to stdout, capture request_id for telemetry.

Smoke tests (what to assert)
- startup returns 200 on /health
- sample chat returns with fields: response, request_id, tokens_used
- streaming endpoint yields incremental chunks (if stream enabled)
- fallback behavior: when we simulate capacity error (env RUN_FALLBACK=1), SDK should retry on compatible model and return 200

Telemetry & Gating
- Telemetry fields emitted by sample: request_id, timestamp, model_name, latency_ms, tokens_in, tokens_out, sdk_version, env (local/demo)
- Default collection: console + local log file; optional push to staging observability if REDWOOD_TELEM_PUSH=true
- Gating: SE should not hand off to customer until smoke tests pass and telemetry events show request_id + tokens_out for >3 requests

Guided demo checklist (1-pager for SE)
- Pre-demo: ensure API key has 500 free tokens or switch to demo-key; run ./smoke-check.sh
- 0–2 minutes: show README-mini.md and explain goals
- 2–6 minutes: start sample-app, run one chat, show logs + token breakdown
- 6–9 minutes: flip RUN_FALLBACK=1 to demonstrate graceful degradation
- 9–10 minutes: share link to GH sample and invite the dev to run on their laptop

Hand-off to Solutions (what to attach)
- ZIP of pico-kit or GH link + branch + PR to main (if modified)
- short Loom (2–3 minutes) showing run-local sequence (recorded)
- linear ticket template filled: "Pico kit run + smoke green -> proceed to seed integration"

Developer UX notes / copy suggestions (short)
- CLI messages should be affirmative: "Started local server on http://localhost:3000 — try curl..."
- Error messages: include request_id and clear next steps: "Quota reached (request_id=...) — try demo-fallback or contact se-alerts"

Security & privacy (mini)
- Do NOT log API keys; only log redacted key hashes.
- Telemetry sample must be GDPR-friendly: omit user email, IPs in demo logs.

Open questions / TODOs
- Do we want a single-language canonical or two (Node + Python)? (PRO: reach, CON: maintenance)
- Decide which model variant to pin in the sample (recommend: small/fast open model verified by runtime team).
- Add automated local dev env for Windows (PowerShell variants).

Action items (owners)
- Maya: finalize README-mini and the smoke-check.sh (deadline: 2025-02-09)
- Liam: add sample telemetry push stub to staging observability (LINEAR:DX-412)
- Zoe: record 2-min loom and push to GH PR as demo asset

References / Links
- Quick canvas: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/DEV/quick-onboard-canvas
- Starter GH: https://github.com/redwood-inference/pico-kit
- Related linear tickets: DX-391 (pico kit), DX-412 (telemetry push)
- Slack channels: #devexp, #sdk-help (ping @oncall-se for demo slots)

Notes-to-self
- Keep examples as close to real usage as possible: streaming + cost breakdown is the 'aha'.
- Avoid heavy config; aim for one env var (REDWOOD_API_KEY) + one flag for fallback.

End of sketch — looking for feedback on the two-language tradeoff and whether to include a tiny React client (probably not — keep it CLI/server only).
